note: General diecast reference for Hoardr. The brands layer grounds scale, tier and typical value for any diecast item; notable is a short set of collector highlights. Values are indicative and vary by condition, box and market; the real measure is recent comparable sales.

brands.name: Dinky Toys
brands.typical: A$40 to A$600, pre-war and rare Supertoys into the thousands
brands.notes: The original mass diecast car. Pre-war and 1950s Supertoys most valuable; watch for zinc pest in pre-1960 castings.

brands.name: Corgi Toys
brands.typical: A$30 to A$500, film and TV tie-ins into the thousands
brands.notes: The ones with windows. James Bond and Batman film cars are the most collectible; boxed originals command a premium.

brands.name: Matchbox
brands.typical: A$5 to A$60, rare Lesney regular-wheels variants into the hundreds or thousands
brands.notes: Lesney regular-wheels era (1953 to 1969) is the collector sweet spot; Superfast from 1969. Colour variants and boxes drive value.

brands.name: Oxford Diecast
brands.notes: Detailed British outline models; 1:76 (OO) suits model railways.

brands.name: Lledo
brands.notes: Nostalgic vintage commercials and promotionals.

brands.name: Spot-On
brands.notes: Tri-ang's constant-scale British range; scarce and sought after.

brands.name: Amalgam
brands.notes: Hand-built museum-grade replicas, often licensed by manufacturers.

brands.name: Hot Wheels
brands.typical: A$3 to A$30 mainline; Redlines, Treasure Hunts and RLC into the hundreds or thousands
brands.notes: Best-selling toy car. Redline era (1968 to 1977), chase cars and error casts are the collectible end; the Beach Bomb prototype is the grail.

brands.name: Greenlight
brands.notes: Licensed TV and film replicas plus limited editions with strong pop-culture appeal.

brands.name: Johnny Lightning
brands.notes: Hot Wheels rival; vintage Topper-era and limited runs collected.

brands.name: Ertl
brands.notes: Strong in farm and agriculture diecast; 1:16 tractors are a collector niche.

brands.name: Franklin Mint
brands.notes: Mail-order high-detail diecast; values depend on model and completeness of paperwork.

brands.name: Jada Toys
brands.notes: Pop-culture licensed cars, strongest on Fast & Furious.

brands.name: M2 Machines
brands.notes: Detailed American classics in 1:64 with chase variants.

brands.name: First Gear
brands.notes: Trucks and commercials; overlaps the construction and haulage niche.

brands.name: Tomica
brands.typical: A$5 to A$25 mainline; Tomica Limited Vintage A$30 to A$150
brands.notes: Japan's everyday small-scale brand; TLV is the collector-grade line.

brands.name: Kyosho
brands.notes: Meticulous Japanese and European sports cars; serious collector brand.

brands.name: AUTOart
brands.notes: Among the most detailed 1:18 diecast; opening everything, fine interiors.

brands.name: Ebbro
brands.notes: Japanese road and racing subjects often overlooked elsewhere.

brands.name: Mini GT
brands.notes: Premium 1:64 by TSM; strong on JDM and tuner subjects.

brands.name: Diapet
brands.notes: Yonezawa's long-running Japanese range; vintage examples collected.

brands.name: Siku
brands.notes: German everyday cars and commercials; 1:32 Siku Farmer is a big agriculture niche.

brands.name: Minichamps
brands.notes: Paul's Model Art; vast road and motorsport catalogue, often limited numbered runs.

brands.name: Schuco
brands.notes: Historic German maker; classic cars and the tiny Piccolo range.

brands.name: CMC
brands.notes: Museum-grade classic and racing models with hundreds of parts.

brands.name: NZG
brands.notes: Construction, crane and commercial models; overlaps the mining and plant niche.

brands.name: Conrad
brands.notes: Construction and commercial vehicles in 1:50.

brands.name: Schabak
brands.notes: German promotionals, often VW and Porsche.

brands.name: Norev
brands.notes: French classics and everyday European cars; good value detail.

brands.name: Solido
brands.notes: Long-running French maker; classics and military.

brands.name: Majorette
brands.notes: France's everyday small-scale brand; vintage France-made examples collected.

brands.name: Spark
brands.notes: Resin, not diecast; motorsport and limited editions in fine detail.

brands.name: Eligor
brands.notes: French classics and commercials.

brands.name: Bburago
brands.notes: Affordable entry into 1:18; Ferrari licence is a mainstay.

brands.name: BBR
brands.notes: High-end resin Ferraris and supercars, limited numbered.

brands.name: Looksmart
brands.notes: Hand-built resin, strong on Ferrari and modern supercars.

brands.name: Polistil
brands.notes: Italian vintage ranges in several scales.

brands.name: GT Spirit
brands.notes: Sealed-body resin 1:18 in limited numbered runs; no opening parts.

brands.name: TrueScale (TSM)
brands.notes: Collector resin and diecast; parent of Mini GT.

brands.name: WSI Models
brands.notes: Trucks, cranes and plant in 1:50; overlaps the construction and haulage niche.

brands.name: Universal Hobbies
brands.notes: Agriculture (1:32) and construction; licensed tractor ranges.

brands.name: Diecast Masters
brands.notes: Official Caterpillar licensee (took over from Norscot); the construction and mining mainstay.

brands.name: Norscot
brands.notes: Former Caterpillar licensee before Diecast Masters; collected secondhand.

notable.why: The rear-loading prototype is the most valuable production-era Hot Wheels, a handful known.

notable.modelName: Corgi gold-plated James Bond Lotus Esprit (presentation)
notable.why: One-off gold-plated presentation piece; standard versions are far less.
First-year Redline; rare colours and a no-paint example have sold in the thousands.

notable.modelName: Corgi 261 James Bond Aston Martin DB5
notable.why: The original Bond car with ejector seat; boxed with figures most valuable.
Sought-after advertising livery; a boxed example made GBP 1,100 at auction.
Lesney regular-wheels crane; rare colour variants command strong premiums.
Pre-war Dinky; condition and absence of zinc pest are everything.
Film and TV tie-in; boxed with figures and accessories most valuable.
